questions.stem: Why does the temperature remain constant during a change of state, even though energy is being supplied?

options.text: The thermometer stops working at the melting point
The energy is used to overcome forces between particles rather than increasing kinetic energy
The particles stop moving during a change of state
The energy is being lost to the surroundings

questions.explanation: During a change of state, the energy being supplied is used to overcome the forces between particles (breaking intermolecular bonds), not to increase the kinetic energy of the particles. Since temperature is a measure of kinetic energy, the temperature stays constant until the state change is complete. This energy is called latent heat.

questions.stem: What is the difference between evaporation and boiling?

options.text: Evaporation only happens to water, while boiling can happen to any liquid
Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature, while boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point
Evaporation absorbs energy while boiling releases energy
There is no difference; they are the same process

questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs at the surface of a liquid at any temperature and is a slow process. Boiling occurs throughout the liquid but only at the boiling point, is a fast process, and produces bubbles. Both involve the change from liquid to gas, but they differ in where and when they occur.
